additions.statement: Light conditions were four-hundred times less than terrestrial conditions.
additions.corrects: Light conditions were five-hundred times less than terrestrial conditions.
additions.reason: Uranus is about 19 AU out, giving roughly 1/400 sunlight.

additions.statement: Closest approach to Uranus took place at 17:59 UT Jan. 24, 1986, at a range of about 50,640 kilometers (31,500 miles).
additions.corrects: at 17:59 ED Jan. 24, 1968, at a range of about 50,640 kilometers (81,500 miles)
additions.reason: Flyby was 1986; 50,640 km is about 31,500 miles.

additions.statement: given such names as Puck, Portia, Juliet, Cressida, Rosalind, Belinda, Desdemona, Cordelia, Ophelia, and Bianca - obvious allusions to Shakespeare, continuing a naming tradition begun in 1852

additions.reason: These are Shakespearean names; Ariel and Umbriel were named 1852.

additions.statement: three new rings in addition to the "older" nine rings, and a magnetic field tilted at 55 degrees off-axis and off-center
additions.corrects: three new rings in addition to the "older" eight rings, and a magnetic field tilted at 66 degrees
additions.reason: Nine rings were known pre-Voyager; the tilt is about 55 degrees.

additions.statement: wind speeds in Uranus' atmosphere as high as 450 km/h (450000 meters per hour)
a boiling lake of water some 497 miles (800 kilometers) below the top cloud surface
additions.corrects: some 479 miles (900 kilometers) below the top cloud surface
additions.reason: The depth is 800 km, which is about 497 miles.

additions.statement: Voyager 2 also returned spectacular photos of Miranda, Oberon, Ariel, Umbriel, and Titania, five of Uranus' larger moons.
additions.corrects: Miranda, Oberon, Ariele, Umbrella, and Titan, five of Uranus' smaller moons
additions.reason: Ariel, Umbriel and Titania are the correct names and the largest moons.

additions.statement: the spacecraft came closest to any object so far in its nearly decade-long travels
additions.reason: Voyager 2 launched in 1977, about nine years before the flyby.

additions.statement: the tragic Challenger accident that killed seven astronauts during their space shuttle launch Jan. 28, 1986
additions.corrects: killed six astronauts during their space shuttle launch Feb. 28, 1986
additions.reason: Challenger broke up on Jan. 28, 1986, killing seven crew.
